phase1_assignment.objective: Audit generic reproducible agent-lifecycle patterns for durable evidence, provenance, continuation, verification and handoff of only irreducible exclusive actions.

observations.mechanism: a physical-science exclusive-action boundary can be represented as independently owned human/instrument authority rather than routine delegation
observations.evidence: Wang et al. (arXiv:2606.27231, submitted 2026-06-25) deploy an LLM-written ARTIQ control stack on real trapped-ion hardware. Every hardware call passes a per-call authorization gate and no call reaches hardware without a token bound to its exact contents. Automatic tokens require isolated dax.sim execution plus per-device bound checks; sensitive or indeterminate actions are blocked by default and escalated to human manual review. The system was deployed on a co-trapped Ca+/CaOH+ platform, interface-validated on an independent Yb+ platform, and red-teamed with 1,932 bench scripts plus approximately 250 harness-level tests. This is direct physical-science evidence that some actions can remain local/automatic while genuinely exclusive sensitive authorization remains outside the agent.
observations.scope: Direct evidence for the existence and machine-checkable structure of an exclusive human authorization boundary on real quantum hardware. It is not a matched comparison of authority-minimal handoff versus always-human or routine delegation, and the filter guarantees hardware-bound compliance rather than scientific sensibility.

observations.mechanism: authorization freshness is a separate lifecycle invariant from action-content binding
observations.evidence: The same trapped-ion system caches approvals for byte-identical scripts. The paper states that cached approval does not expire automatically; after bounds are tightened, the operator must manually invalidate the outstanding approval because the filter does not detect which cached entries are stale. Thus exact-action binding alone is insufficient when the policy/safety envelope changes after authorization.
observations.scope: Observed limitation of this specific authorization cache design; supports binding approval to a policy/bounds revision or equivalent invalidation evidence, not a universal claim that all token systems have this bug.

observations.mechanism: preserve raw failed artifacts for provenance, but normally hand downstream a bounded typed failure record rather than the full raw trajectory
observations.evidence: Negative Knowledge as Failure-aware Shared Memory for AutoResearch (arXiv:2606.21024) uses a separate curator over frozen executed code/output/reasoning artifacts. On 38 deterministic-evaluation ScienceAgentBench tasks with Claude Sonnet 4.6, Base and plain Retry each score 31.6%; one structured negative-knowledge record reaches 36.8% using 296 tokens; three rounds of raw self-debug reach 44.7% using 1,109 tokens; a single deep record distilled from three failed rounds reaches 47.4% using 795 tokens. In a BKdV mathematical-physics loop, Base solves 0/3 new tasks, positive-only 1/3, negative-only 3/3, and positive+negative 3/3 under deterministic physics-aware checks. Cross-system BKdV-only memory solves 2/4 Burgers-NLS tasks versus 0/4 with no bank, but also causes negative transfer on one task. The official reproduction tree bundles logs/banks/prompts/eval scripts and verify-only scripts reporting 31/31, 20/20 and 54/54 paper claims matched across its three studies.
observations.scope: Matched evidence for structured failure-memory payloads in scientific coding and numerical mathematical physics. Sample sizes are small and the evidence does not isolate immutable raw storage itself as the causal factor; it instead argues against handing full raw trajectories downstream by default.

inferences.proposal: Distinguish delegated authority from independently owned exclusive authority. For ordinary delegation, receiver scope cannot exceed sender-owned task authority. For a real missing credential, human approval, or exclusive instrument authority, the receiver may possess a capability the sender deliberately lacks; the admissible scope is then the intersection of task-required capability and receiver capability, with exact action binding and no unrelated authority.

Raw failed/abandoned artifacts remain immutable and addressable at the provenance/replay layer, but the normal handoff payload should be a bounded typed negative-knowledge record derived from those artifacts. A downstream agent must explicitly adopt or reject that record. Full raw trajectory expansion is an on-demand audit/re-derivation operation, not the default context payload.

Authorization must bind not only to the exact canonical action and immutable input digests but also to the effective authorization/safety-policy revision. A changed bounds/policy revision invalidates prior authorization unless an explicit reconciliation/revalidation receipt proves continued validity.

local_execution.schema_result: all 15 mutated packets remain structurally valid under Draft 2020-12; failures are produced by cross-field semantic invariants rather than accidental schema invalidity

unverified_claims: No matched physical-science study was found in this invocation that isolates authority-minimal handoff itself against routine delegation or always-human approval while holding model, task and tools constant.

The trapped-ion token system demonstrates real exclusive human authorization and deterministic hardware protection, but does not verify whether an experiment is scientifically sensible; some measurement-conditioned branches also remain outside automatic certification.

The prior synthesis that downstream agents should receive raw failed branches is too strong. Current matched evidence supports immutable raw source preservation for audit/re-derivation plus bounded typed negative records for normal handoff; raw branch storage itself remains causally unisolated.

Negative-knowledge transfer can mislead when domain mechanics differ, so typed failure memory requires relevance qualification and explicit adopt/reject behavior rather than unconditional enforcement.
